findings.title: Pin and verify the downloaded installer
findings.whyItBreaks: This newly executes whatever https://example.com/install.sh serves during every image build. A changed or compromised remote response can execute arbitrary code in the build environment and makes releases non-reproducible.

findings.title: Pin and verify the downloaded installer
findings.whyItBreaks: Building the image fetches and executes whatever content this URL serves at build time as root. A compromised or changed upstream response can silently execute arbitrary code in the build environment and ship it in the image.

findings.title: Pin and verify the installer before executing it
findings.whyItBreaks: The newly added build step downloads mutable network content and pipes it directly to a shell. A changed or compromised installer can execute arbitrary commands during image construction and alter the resulting image.

findings.title: Preserve missing-key errors in LoadOrDefault
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported helper discards Load's ErrMissing and returns "" for an absent key, making it indistinguishable from a present key with an empty value for external consumers.

findings.title: Preserve the missing-key error in the public API
findings.whyItBreaks: The new exported wrapper discards Load's ErrMissing and returns "" for an absent key, identical to a present key with an empty-string value. Consumers cannot distinguish failure from valid data.

findings.title: Preserve missing-key status in LoadOrDefault
findings.whyItBreaks: The new exported function discards the error from Load. Since Load returns "" with ErrMissing for absent keys, both an absent key and a present key containing "" produce the same result, preventing callers from detecting missing data.

findings.title: Wait for result sends before Run returns
findings.whyItBreaks: The changed goroutines are not joined, so Run can return before result sends complete. A caller that closes results after Run returns can trigger "send on closed channel", and callers can no longer treat return as completion.

findings.title: Wait for result sends before returning
findings.whyItBreaks: The changed goroutine at lines 7-9 allows Run to return while sends to results are still pending. A caller that treats Run's return as completion and closes results can cause a background send to panic with "send on closed channel".

findings.title: Wait for result sends before returning
findings.whyItBreaks: Run now starts sends in goroutines and immediately exits its loop, so callers can observe incomplete results after Run returns or close their results channel and cause a send-on-closed-channel panic.

findings.title: Preserve the original function type for callback consumers
findings.whyItBreaks: Changing Log from func(string) to func(string, ...string) breaks downstream code that uses logger.Log where a func(string) is required, causing an upgrade-time compilation failure even though direct one-argument calls still compile.

findings.whyItBreaks: Using || permits any non-admin user to delete records in their tenant, and permits an admin from a different tenant to delete that tenant's record. Both paths bypass the prior deletion authorization requirement.

findings.title: Restore admin and tenant requirements for record deletion
findings.whyItBreaks: The changed `||` predicate authorizes deletion when either condition holds. An admin from another tenant passes `isAdmin`, and a non-admin in the record's tenant passes the tenant comparison; the base revision required both.

findings.title: Require admin status and tenant match for deletion
findings.whyItBreaks: The changed `||` expression returns true for a non-admin session whose tenant matches the record, bypassing the prior requirement that deletion callers be administrators.

findings.title: Preserve parse failures when updating settings
findings.whyItBreaks: The catch converts malformed or schema-invalid stored settings into defaults. updateFontSize then treats that fallback as valid and calls save with `{theme:"light",fontSize:size}`, whereas it previously propagated the parse error and performed no write. This silently replaces the user's stored settings when only changing font size.

findings.title: Preserve invalid-settings failures
findings.whyItBreaks: The new catch at src/settings.ts:14-15 converts JSON and validation errors to defaults. updateFontSize at src/settings.ts:20 then overwrites and saves invalid stored settings; for example, "{}" is persisted as a valid light-theme settings object instead of surfacing the invalid input.

findings.title: Preserve parse failures instead of overwriting settings
findings.whyItBreaks: The new catch converts malformed or schema-invalid saved settings into defaults. The same-file consumer at src/settings.ts:20-22 then updates the font size and saves those defaults, replacing an invalid saved theme with "light" instead of surfacing the parse/validation error.

findings.title: Use the requested branch commit for artifact lookup
findings.whyItBreaks: The report resolves `builtFrom` from the requested branch, but the changed code fetches artifacts from the separate `verified` ref. If those refs differ, the returned report labels one commit while returning another commit's artifacts.

findings.title: Use the reported commit when loading artifacts
findings.whyItBreaks: buildReport returns builtFrom from build.ref(branch), but the changed return expression loads artifacts from build.ref("verified"). When those refs differ, callers receive artifacts for verified while the report identifies the requested branch commit.

findings.title: Use the reported branch commit to select artifacts
findings.whyItBreaks: `builtFrom` remains the requested branch's commit, but `artifacts` are read from the separate `verified` ref. When those refs differ, the returned report misattributes verified artifacts to the branch commit.

findings.title: Restore the requested entry limit
findings.whyItBreaks: For any positive limit smaller than all.length, this returns every entry rather than at most limit. renderFeed passes 20 at src/feed.ts:9, so 21 entries produce a 21-item result.

findings.title: Respect the requested entry limit
findings.whyItBreaks: For any positive limit smaller than all.length, this returns every reversed entry instead of at most limit entries. renderFeed requests 20 entries at src/feed.ts:9, so inputs longer than 20 expand its output beyond 20 entries.

findings.title: Restore the requested entry limit
findings.whyItBreaks: For any positive limit smaller than all.length, this returns every entry despite the documented at-most-limit contract. src/feed.ts:9 calls it with 20 and iterates page.length, so feeds with more than 20 entries produce more than 20 output entries.

findings.title: Count only emitted manifest entries
findings.whyItBreaks: The new filtering omits stale entries from rows, but the header still receives entries.length. Output containing stale entries therefore declares more entries than it emits.

findings.title: Count only emitted manifest entries
findings.whyItBreaks: When an entry has stale=true, it is omitted from rows but still included in headerLines(opts, entries.length). Two input entries with one stale produce '# entry-count: 2' followed by one data row.

findings.title: Count only emitted manifest rows
findings.whyItBreaks: The new filter on line 20 omits stale entries from rows, while the header still receives entries.length. This produces a manifest whose declared entry count exceeds its emitted data rows.

findings.title: Restore execute's string result
findings.whyItBreaks: Every call to the exported execute(input): string function now throws, so the supported uppercase-result path is unusable.

findings.title: Preserve the viewer read-only outcome
findings.whyItBreaks: The new `req.role === "viewer"` rejection prevents active viewers below the attempt limit from reaching `handle`'s existing `"read-only"` branch at src/handler.ts:24. They now receive `"rejected"`.

findings.title: Allow eligible viewers to reach read-only handling
findings.whyItBreaks: An active viewer with fewer than five attempts previously reached handle()'s explicit "read-only" outcome, but isEligible() now rejects it first, so handle() returns "rejected" instead.

findings.title: Preserve the viewer read-only path

findings.title: Keep saving drafts independent of payment
findings.whyItBreaks: The changed predicate at src/policy.ts:7 returns false for a draft with payment="missing". Its consumer at src/actions.ts:9 therefore returns "blocked" instead of "saved", preventing persistence of an unpaid draft.

findings.title: Keep payment checks out of draft saves
findings.whyItBreaks: Adding `order.payment === "paid"` to the shared predicate makes `saveDraft({ state: "draft", payment: "missing" })` return "blocked". Saving a draft is independently legitimate before payment, so this regresses the draft-saving path.

findings.title: Keep draft saving independent of payment
findings.whyItBreaks: `canProceed` is also the gate for `saveDraft`. A draft with `payment: "missing"` now returns `"blocked"`, preventing users from saving a legitimately incomplete draft.

findings.title: Read files from the published channel commit
findings.whyItBreaks: The returned Snapshot sets commit to headCommit(channel), but its files come from headCommit("stable"). Publishing any non-stable channel therefore returns files that do not match the snapshot's reported commit and channel.

findings.title: Keep snapshot files aligned with its commit
findings.whyItBreaks: The returned Snapshot reports the requested channel's head in `commit` but loads `files` from `stable`. When those refs differ, the snapshot's metadata and contents describe different revisions.

findings.title: Read snapshot files from the requested channel head
findings.whyItBreaks: For any channel whose head differs from stable, Snapshot.commit identifies that channel's head while Snapshot.files lists stable's contents. Consumers therefore publish or inspect a self-inconsistent snapshot and omit channel-specific changes.

findings.title: Honor the supplied limit
findings.whyItBreaks: `build(prefix, limit=10)` newly presents `limit` as a caller-controlled output bound, but `max_count` remains fixed at 10. Thus `build("x", 3)` returns 10 entries.

findings.title: Apply the supplied limit
findings.whyItBreaks: `build(prefix, limit=10)` newly exposes a caller-controlled result bound, but the implementation still iterates a fixed `max_count = 10`. Thus `build("x", 2)` returns 10 values rather than 2.

findings.title: Honor the new limit parameter
findings.whyItBreaks: `build(prefix, limit=10)` newly exposes caller-controlled result limiting, but the body still uses `max_count = 10`; `build("x", 2)` returns ten values.

findings.title: Enforce positivity in parse_positive_int
findings.whyItBreaks: The renamed public function promises a positive integer, but `int(value)` returns 0 and negative values unchanged. Callers relying on this contract can receive `-1` or `0` as valid parsed results.

findings.title: Validate that parsed integers are positive
findings.whyItBreaks: The renamed parse_positive_int('-1') returns -1 because its body only calls int(). The changed charge path consumes that result and returns -100, violating the newly promised positive-value contract.

findings.title: Reject non-positive inputs in parse_positive_int
findings.whyItBreaks: The renamed function newly promises positive validation, but `int(value)` accepts `0` and negative values. Its changed caller at `src/validators.py:6` therefore turns `-1` into a negative charge.

findings.title: Preserve the input DataFrame instead of mutating it
findings.whyItBreaks: Previously apply_values copied df and returned the transformed copy. The changed assignment writes directly into df, so callers that retain or reuse their input observe unexpected value changes after calling this function.

findings.title: Preserve the caller DataFrame
findings.whyItBreaks: The removed df.copy() means assignments now modify the DataFrame passed by the caller. Previously the function returned transformed data while leaving its input unchanged; callers that reuse df after this call will silently observe modified values.

findings.title: Preserve the caller DataFrame instead of mutating it
findings.whyItBreaks: The previous implementation copied df and updated only that copy. The new assignment writes directly into the caller-owned DataFrame, so code retaining df for reuse, comparison, or rollback observes unexpected changed values after calling apply_values.

findings.title: Enforce positivity in parse_positive_int
findings.whyItBreaks: The new public name promises a positive integer, but "-1" parses successfully and is returned unchanged. The changed consumer at src/parse.rs:6 multiplies that value, producing -100.

findings.title: Validate positivity before returning the parsed amount
findings.whyItBreaks: `parse_positive_int("-1")` returns `-1`, despite its public name promising a positive integer; `charge("-1")` consequently returns `-100`.

findings.title: Avoid moving items before calculating its length
findings.whyItBreaks: `dbg!(items)` evaluates and returns its argument by value, consuming the `Vec<String>`. The following `items.len()` therefore borrows a moved value and produces Rust error E0382.

findings.title: Remove the debug statement that moves `items`
findings.whyItBreaks: `dbg!(items)` consumes and returns `items`; because its return value is discarded here, the subsequent `items.len()` uses a moved `Vec<String>` and fails to compile.

findings.title: Avoid moving items before computing its length
findings.whyItBreaks: `dbg!(items);` consumes the owned `Vec<String>` and drops its returned value. The following `items.len()` uses the moved value, causing Rust error E0382.

findings.title: Compute paths from the declared base revision
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported Changeset contract states that changedPaths are computed against fromRevision so consumers can replay them on that exact revision. This line instead computes paths from the current "latest" revision while returning the pinned revision in fromRevision, producing a mismatched changeset whenever pinnedTag is not latest.

findings.title: Compute changed paths from fromRevision
findings.whyItBreaks: `fromRevision` remains the resolved pinned tag, but `changedPaths` is now read from the separately resolved `latest` revision. This violates the documented Changeset contract that paths were computed against the replay revision.

findings.title: Compute changed paths from the declared base revision
findings.whyItBreaks: When `pinnedTag` resolves to a revision other than `latest`, `changedPaths` describes changes relative to `latest` but `fromRevision` tells consumers to replay those paths on the pinned revision. This violates the exported Changeset contract and can omit paths changed since the pin or include paths unavailable at that revision.

findings.title: Update queries to use the renamed column
findings.whyItBreaks: After this migration, `users.email` no longer exists, while `src/query.sql:1` executes `SELECT email FROM users`. Executing this query after upgrading fails with a missing-column error.

findings.title: Update queries to use the renamed column
findings.whyItBreaks: After this migration, users.email no longer exists, but src/query.sql:1 still executes SELECT email FROM users. Any path using that query will fail with a missing-column database error after upgrade.

findings.title: Update queries that still select the renamed column
findings.whyItBreaks: After this migration, users.email no longer exists, but src/query.sql:1 executes SELECT email FROM users. Any database upgraded through 0002 will fail that query with a missing-column error.

findings.title: Restore environment-based billing credential loading
findings.whyItBreaks: The changed line places a billing key in version control, exposing it to repository readers and commit history. It also replaces the exported makeClient() function's missing-configuration error with a shared key, so deployments without BILLING_API_KEY silently receive that credential.

findings.title: Remove and revoke the committed billing API key
findings.whyItBreaks: The changed line commits a `bk_live_` credential and makes `makeClient()` return it for every invocation, replacing runtime configuration and the missing-key failure.

findings.title: Remove the committed live billing API key
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported `makeClient` now always returns a client containing the committed `bk_live_...` credential. Repository or build-artifact access exposes that live key, and an unset deployment configuration no longer fails safely.

findings.title: Restore admin authorization for project purges
findings.whyItBreaks: The changed guards return "forbidden" when user.isAdmin is true, then call db.delete for any non-admin with an archived project. This permits an unauthorized deletion and rejects authorized administrators.

findings.title: Allow administrators to purge archived projects
findings.whyItBreaks: For user.isAdmin=true and project.archived=true, this branch returns "forbidden" before deletion. The prior implementation purged exactly that combination, so administrators can no longer perform the purge workflow.

findings.title: Restore the admin authorization check
findings.whyItBreaks: The changed guard returns "forbidden" for administrators, then permits any non-admin with an archived project to reach `db.delete(project.id)` and receive "purged". This reverses the prior authorization behavior and permits unauthorized deletion.

findings.title: Restore missing-config fallback
findings.whyItBreaks: load_settings returns None when the path does not exist (app/config.py:6-7). The changed startup path then subscripts None at app/config.py:14, raising TypeError instead of returning the previous default worker count of 1.

findings.title: Restore missing-settings fallback
findings.whyItBreaks: load_settings returns None when the path does not exist (app/config.py:6-7). Removing the fallback makes startup evaluate settings["workers"] on None and raise TypeError, rather than returning the prior default worker count of 1.

findings.title: Preserve defaults when the settings file is missing
findings.whyItBreaks: load_settings returns None for a nonexistent path. The removed fallback means startup indexes None at the changed return line, raising TypeError instead of returning the previous default worker count.

findings.title: Propagate gateway submission failures
findings.whyItBreaks: When Gateway.Submit returns an error, Charge logs it and returns nil. Callers therefore cannot distinguish a declined or failed charge from a successful one and may complete an order without payment.

findings.title: Propagate gateway submission failures
findings.whyItBreaks: The changed error branch logs a Gateway.Submit failure and falls through to `return nil`. As an exported API, Charge now makes rejected payments indistinguishable from successful charges.

findings.title: Propagate gateway submission failures
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported Charge function now logs a Gateway.Submit error at line 17 and then returns nil. Consumers therefore receive a successful result for a failed charge.

findings.title: Include tenantId in the settings cache key
findings.whyItBreaks: The process-global cache now keys entries only by name. Once tenant A caches a setting, tenant B requesting the same name receives that cached value at src/settings.ts:13 without calling store.fetch, leaking or returning incorrect tenant-specific configuration.

findings.title: Restore tenant scoping in cache keys
findings.whyItBreaks: After tenant A caches `name`, a request for the same name in tenant B hits `settings:name` and returns tenant A's value without calling `store.fetch(tenantB, name)`. The base implementation keyed entries by `tenantId` and `name`.

findings.title: Preserve the exported invalidate signature
findings.whyItBreaks: Existing TypeScript consumers calling `invalidate(tenantId, name)` no longer compile. JavaScript callers passing two arguments cause `tenantId` to be treated as the name, deleting `settings:<tenantId>` instead of the requested setting.

findings.title: Include tenant ID in the settings cache key
findings.whyItBreaks: settingsFor still fetches values scoped by tenantId, but cacheKey is derived only from name. After tenant A reads "theme", tenant B reading the same name receives tenant A's cached value without calling store.fetch.

findings.title: Serialize reservations before awaiting persistence
findings.whyItBreaks: The await yields after reading `remaining` but before updating `stock`. With one unit loaded, two concurrent `reserve(sku)` calls both read 1, both save 0, and both return true, allowing two reservations for one unit.

findings.title: Serialize reservations for the same SKU
findings.whyItBreaks: The await yields after reading stock but before updating it. With one unit loaded, two concurrent reserve("sku") calls both read 1, both save 0, both return true, and both represent successful reservations despite only one unit being available.

findings.title: Serialize reservations before awaiting persistence
findings.whyItBreaks: With stock=1, two concurrent reserve calls can both read remaining=1 and reach the await before either call updates the map. Both then persist 0 and return true, approving two reservations for one item.

findings.title: Remove the duplicate milliseconds conversion in retry
findings.whyItBreaks: `backoff(0)` now returns 1,000 milliseconds, but `retry` still multiplies it by 1,000 before sleeping. The first retry therefore waits 1,000,000 ms (~16.7 minutes) instead of the prior 1 second; later retries can wait up to ~8.3 hours.

findings.title: Keep retry delays in the backoff unit
findings.whyItBreaks: `backoff(0)` now returns 1,000 milliseconds, but `retry` multiplies it by 1,000 before calling `sleep` at `src/jobs/retry.ts:12`. The first retry waits 1,000,000 ms instead of 1 second; capped retries wait 30,000,000 ms instead of 30 seconds.

findings.title: Keep retry backoff in milliseconds
findings.whyItBreaks: `backoff(0)` now returns 1,000 milliseconds, but `retry` still multiplies it by 1,000 before sleeping. A first failed retry waits 1,000,000 ms (~16.7 minutes) rather than 1 second; capped retries wait ~8.3 hours.

findings.title: Propagate the file close error from Save
findings.whyItBreaks: The new deferred f.Close() discards its error. Previously, Save returned a close failure after a successful flush, so delayed filesystem write failures can now be reported as a successful Save.

findings.title: Propagate the file close error from Save
findings.whyItBreaks: The new deferred Close result is discarded. If the file reports a persistence failure only on Close after Flush succeeds, Save returns nil even though finalization failed; the base version returned that error.

findings.title: Propagate the file close error
findings.whyItBreaks: The new deferred f.Close() discards its error, while Save now returns w.Flush() directly. A Close failure after a successful flush is therefore reported as nil, unlike the base revision's return f.Close(); callers of this exported API can treat a failed save as successful.

findings.title: Include the page end position in the window
findings.whyItBreaks: The documented half-open bounds are [start, end), but range(start, end - 1) excludes end - 1. Every nonempty page loses its last row; pages of size one render as empty, so summarize also omits rows.

findings.title: Include each page's final row
findings.whyItBreaks: _window_bounds returns a half-open end, but range(start, end - 1) excludes the final valid position. A two-row page returns one row and a one-row final page returns none; render_page and summarize therefore silently omit rows.

findings.title: Include each page's final row
findings.whyItBreaks: The bounds helper defines end as exclusive, but range(start, end - 1) excludes the row at end - 1. As a result, page_window(["a"], 0, 1) returns [], and summarize silently omits the last row of every page.

findings.title: Return cached values only before their TTL expires
findings.whyItBreaks: The expiry comparison is inverted: a newly stored entry has elapsed time near zero and is immediately deleted, while an entry older than ttlMs is returned as valid.

findings.title: Remove all completed jobs without skipping adjacent entries
findings.whyItBreaks: Splicing during forEach shifts the next job into the removed index, but forEach then advances to the following index. Consecutive completed jobs therefore leave every second completed job in the returned queue.

findings.title: Restore the live-entry check
findings.whyItBreaks: A freshly stored entry has elapsed time near zero, which does not satisfy `elapsed > ttlMs` for a positive TTL; `get` deletes it and returns null. Entries older than the TTL are instead returned.

findings.title: Do not splice while iterating completed jobs
findings.whyItBreaks: Splicing shifts the next job into the current index while `forEach` advances. For `[done, done]`, the second completed job remains in the returned queue.

findings.title: Preserve pruneDone's non-mutating result contract
findings.whyItBreaks: The prior implementation returned a filtered copy. This change mutates the caller-provided `jobs` array, so callers retaining that array lose completed jobs as an unintended side effect.

findings.title: Restore the non-expired TTL comparison
findings.whyItBreaks: A newly stored entry has age near zero, so for a normal positive ttlMs the new `>` condition deletes it and returns null. Conversely, entries older than ttlMs are returned as valid cache hits.

findings.title: Do not splice while iterating done jobs
findings.whyItBreaks: `forEach` advances its index after `splice` shifts the next element left. For `[done, done]`, removing index 0 causes the second done job to move to index 0, then it is skipped; `pruneDone` returns a completed job.

findings.title: Use a numeric comparator when sorting scores
findings.whyItBreaks: Array.sort() compares scores as strings. For players ordered [{score: 2}, {score: 10}] with n=1, rankScores produces [2, 10], making cutoff 2; filtering and slicing then returns the score-2 player instead of the score-10 player. formatBoard consequently displays the wrong leader.

findings.title: Sort scores numerically before reversing
findings.whyItBreaks: Array.sort() compares numbers as strings, so scores [2, 10, 9] become [10, 2, 9] before reversal and produce cutoff 2 for n=2. topPlayers can then return a score-2 player while excluding score 9.

findings.title: Sort scores numerically before reversing
findings.whyItBreaks: Array#sort() without a comparator compares scores as strings. With scores [9, 10, 8], rankScores returns [9, 8, 10]; for n=1, topPlayers uses 9 as the cutoff and returns the 9-point player before the 10-point player.

findings.title: Use a constant-time signature comparison
findings.whyItBreaks: String equality can exit after the first differing character, exposing comparison-time differences to an attacker submitting repeated webhook requests. This weakens the HMAC verification performed before handle() authorizes processor(payload).

findings.title: Restore constant-time webhook signature comparison
findings.whyItBreaks: The changed `==` comparison may return earlier for differing signature prefixes, allowing remote webhook callers to measure verification time through `handle`'s response and potentially build a signature timing oracle. This replaces the prior constant-time comparison.

findings.title: Restore constant-time signature comparison
findings.whyItBreaks: `==` may stop at the first mismatch, revealing signature-prefix timing information to webhook callers. A valid comparison reaches the authenticated processor path at `app/webhook.py:14`; use `hmac.compare_digest` to avoid exposing this signal.

findings.title: Keep ledger and balance updates in one transaction
findings.whyItBreaks: The changed line invokes `_apply_balances` after the `db.transaction()` block has exited. If either balance UPDATE raises, the ledger insert has already committed; if the second UPDATE raises, the source debit may also persist without the destination credit.

findings.title: Keep balance updates inside the transfer transaction
findings.whyItBreaks: The changed line invokes `_apply_balances` only after the `db.transaction()` block has exited and committed the ledger insert. If either balance UPDATE raises, the ledger entry remains committed although the transfer did not complete. Move the balance updates into the transaction block so the ledger and balances roll back together.

findings.title: Keep ledger and both balance updates in one transaction
findings.whyItBreaks: The transaction ends before `_apply_balances` runs. If either balance update fails, the ledger insert remains committed while account balances are only partly updated or unchanged; the base revision rolled back all three writes together.

findings.title: Keep billing-day calculation in UTC
findings.whyItBreaks: The prior implementation explicitly used UTC fields. The new local-time fields produce a different billing key near midnight depending on the host timezone; for example, 2026-01-01T00:30:00Z becomes 2025-12-31 in America/Los_Angeles. This also changes sameBillingDay results across a UTC boundary.

findings.title: Preserve UTC semantics for billing-day keys
findings.whyItBreaks: The changed return uses local-time getters whereas the prior implementation used UTC getters. On a host in America/Los_Angeles, 2026-01-01T00:30:00Z now produces 2025-12-31 instead of 2026-01-01, changing billing-day keys by deployment time zone.

findings.title: Preserve UTC calendar extraction
findings.whyItBreaks: The changed line replaces UTC getters with local-time getters. A UTC instant near midnight can now be assigned to the previous or next billing day depending on the server timezone.

findings.title: Restore tenant scoping in the profile cache key
findings.whyItBreaks: After readProfile("tenant-a", "alice", ...) caches tenant-a's profile, readProfile("tenant-b", "alice", ...) returns that cached profile without calling fetchProfile. The returned Profile includes its tenant, so this leaks incorrect cross-tenant data.

findings.title: Restore tenant isolation in the profile cache key
findings.whyItBreaks: Two tenants with the same account value now use the same memo entry. After one tenant's profile is cached, readProfile for the other tenant returns that cached Profile without calling fetchProfile, exposing incorrect cross-tenant profile data.

findings.title: Include tenant in the profile cache key
findings.whyItBreaks: After caching profile (tenant="a", account="x"), a later read for (tenant="b", account="x") uses the same key and returns tenant a's Profile without invoking fetchProfile.

findings.title: Preserve missing-key errors from load
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported load API previously propagated a missing-key Error, but now catches it and returns "". Callers cannot distinguish a failed lookup from a stored empty string, so missing data can silently be accepted as valid data.

findings.title: Preserve missing-key errors
findings.whyItBreaks: A missing key previously threw `Error("missing: <key>")`; it now returns `""`, which is a valid stored value. `loadAll` consequently returns a normal-looking array containing an empty string and cannot distinguish a missing key from an intentionally empty value.

findings.title: Preserve missing-key failures
findings.whyItBreaks: The new catch returns "" for a missing key, making absence indistinguishable from a key explicitly stored with an empty string. Exported loadAll consequently returns successful-looking data for missing entries.

findings.title: Preserve the existing Config timeout field
findings.whyItBreaks: Existing consumers passing the previously required `timeoutMs` property no longer type-check; untyped consumers pass `undefined` as `config.timeout`, making the deadline NaN so the timeout guard never stops retries. The newly required `retries` property also breaks existing Config literals even though retry() does not use it.

findings.title: Propagate terminal background retry failures
findings.whyItBreaks: When every attempt throws, retryBackground returns void exactly as it does after a successful attempt. As an exported API, this forces every caller to treat failure as success and can let subsequent work proceed after the callback never completed.

findings.title: Preserve the existing Config fields
findings.whyItBreaks: Existing consumers passing the published `{ maxAttempts, timeoutMs }` configuration no longer type-check because `timeoutMs` was removed and `retries` is newly required. Untyped existing consumers instead compute `Date.now() + undefined`, yielding `NaN`; the deadline comparison is then always false, so `retry` no longer honors their timeout.

findings.title: Make retryBackground actually run in the background
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported `retryBackground` contract promises background work, but it directly invokes `fn()` in a synchronous loop. A slow callback blocks the caller and cannot execute independently in the background.

findings.title: Report retryBackground exhaustion to its caller
findings.whyItBreaks: After every callback attempt throws, the catch discards the error and the exported function returns `undefined`, indistinguishable from success. Callers cannot distinguish an exhausted background operation from a completed one.

findings.title: Preserve the existing Config timeout contract
findings.whyItBreaks: This exported interface removes required `timeoutMs`, adds required `retries`, and renames the timeout property. Existing TypeScript callers of `retry` no longer type-check. Existing JavaScript callers still passing `timeoutMs` make `config.timeout` undefined, so the deadline becomes NaN and the timeout guard never stops retries.

findings.title: Expose background retry exhaustion to callers
findings.whyItBreaks: The new exported API catches every callback failure and returns `void` both after success and after all retries fail. Its callers are forced to treat exhaustion as success and cannot safely avoid acting on a failed background operation.

findings.title: Handle numeric Field values before reading length
findings.whyItBreaks: FieldProps now publicly accepts number, but the changed expression reads value.length, which is invalid for the number branch and rejects type-checking. At runtime, numeric values produce len=undefined.

findings.title: Handle numeric values before reading length
findings.whyItBreaks: `FieldProps.value` now accepts `number`, but `value.length` is invalid for numbers. This produces a TypeScript error and would render `len=undefined` for numeric values if type errors are emitted.

findings.title: Support numeric Field values before widening the public prop
findings.whyItBreaks: `FieldProps` now permits numbers, but `Field` reads `value.length`. TypeScript rejects this because numbers have no `length`; numeric callers would otherwise produce `len=undefined`.

findings.title: Remove the token from workflow output
findings.whyItBreaks: The added command expands $TOKEN, sourced from secrets.TOKEN, into the CI job log.

findings.title: Restore the Git diff output buffer limit
findings.whyItBreaks: `git()` now uses Node's default 1 MiB `spawnSync` buffer. `runGithub` reads the complete PR patch through this helper at `src/adapters/github.ts:140`, so a PR with more than 1 MiB of diff output fails before review posting instead of supporting the previous 64 MiB limit.

findings.title: Preserve capacity for large Git diffs
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing `maxBuffer` restores Node's 1 MiB default. A larger patch from the changed `git diff` call exceeds it, causing `spawnSync` to fail before review generation.

findings.title: Retain a buffer large enough for PR diffs
findings.whyItBreaks: `git()` produces the full patch at src/adapters/github.ts:140. Without `maxBuffer`, `spawnSync` uses Node's 1 MiB default; a larger textual diff causes the child process to fail, preventing review completion.

findings.title: Restore the read-only sandbox for Codex runs
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing `-s read-only` makes this wrapper inherit Codex's configured sandbox policy. If that policy is `workspace-write`, model-generated commands can modify `opts.repoPath`, which is passed as the working directory. The wrapper previously enforced read-only behavior and exposes no sandbox override to callers.

findings.title: Restore the mandatory read-only sandbox
findings.whyItBreaks: runCodex passes its prompt directly to Codex with opts.repoPath as the working directory. Removing -s read-only means this runner no longer enforces inspection-only execution, so a review invocation can modify the repository when Codex uses a writable sandbox default or configuration.

findings.title: Keep the Codex sandbox pinned to read-only
findings.whyItBreaks: The changed argument list no longer passes `-s read-only`, so `codex exec` can inherit a less restrictive sandbox configuration. This runner executes with `cwd: opts.repoPath`; a workspace-write configuration can therefore allow a review run to modify the repository, removing the prior technical non-writing boundary.

findings.title: Compute the review diff from the PR merge base and head
findings.whyItBreaks: The changed lines diff `baseSha` against the checkout's `HEAD` while the bundle still reports the independently supplied `headSha`. When the checkout is a merge ref or the target branch advanced after divergence, the patch and changed-file set can include target-only changes and no longer match the declared PR head.

findings.title: Diff from the PR merge-base, not the current base tip
findings.whyItBreaks: PR_BASE_SHA may be a target-branch commit newer than the PR's fork point. When HEAD is the PR head, `git diff baseSha HEAD` compares unrelated branch tips, so base-only commits appear as inverse changes in both the review patch and changed-file set. Needlefish can then review/comment on files not changed by the PR.

findings.title: Build the bundle from the PR head and merge base
findings.whyItBreaks: The Bundle advertises `headSha`, but the new patch and changed-file range use the checkout's `HEAD`. If `PR_HEAD_SHA` differs from the checkout ref, the review content no longer corresponds to the commit receiving the review. Directly diffing from `PR_BASE_SHA` can also include base-only changes when that SHA is not an ancestor of the PR head.

findings.title: Preserve prompt payloads with callback replacements
findings.whyItBreaks: The changed string replacement arguments interpret `$&`, `$`` and `$'` as String.replace substitution tokens. Since bundle JSON, candidate findings, and bundle.patch may contain arbitrary source text, these sequences are rewritten before being sent to Codex, silently corrupting the prompt.

findings.title: Preserve literal prompt content during placeholder replacement
findings.whyItBreaks: The changed string replacements interpret replacement tokens such as $&, $`, $', and $$ in serialized bundle/candidate content or bundle.patch. Source text containing those tokens is therefore altered before it is supplied to the reviewer or critic.

findings.title: Preserve literal dollar sequences in prompt payloads
findings.whyItBreaks: String.prototype.replace interprets $&, $`, $', and $$ in string replacements. A bundle patch containing "$&" is rewritten to "{{BUNDLE}}" before it reaches runCodex; "$`" can inject the prompt prefix. The same changed string-replacement form is used for candidate JSON and the patch in the critic prompt.

findings.title: Preserve commit_id in the fallback review request
findings.whyItBreaks: The review result is computed from `headSha` (the patch is built at lines 141-144), but the fallback now omits `commit_id`. GitHub defaults an omitted `commit_id` to the PR's most recent commit. If a new commit is pushed while review() is running and the initial request fails (for example because inline comments are rejected), the fallback posts REQUEST_CHANGES or COMMENT against that newer, unreviewed commit.

findings.title: Keep the analyzed SHA in fallback reviews
findings.whyItBreaks: The changed fallback request omits commit_id, so GitHub attaches it to the PR's current head. The review content was computed from headSha captured at src/adapters/github.ts:141 and passed at src/adapters/github.ts:183; if the PR advances before fallback, the stale verdict is recorded against the new commit.

findings.title: Keep the fallback review pinned to the reviewed commit
findings.whyItBreaks: If the JSON review request fails, this fallback omits `commit_id`. GitHub then associates the review with the PR's latest commit, so a commit pushed after `headSha` was reviewed can receive that stale verdict.

findings.title: Reject malformed findings instead of fabricating findings
findings.whyItBreaks: Invalid fields that previously raised a malformed-finding error now become plausible-looking output: an invalid severity becomes P1, an invalid category becomes bug, and missing locations become file="" with lineStart/lineEnd=0. Callers of this exported normalizer can no longer distinguish a failed review parse from a real finding, so malformed model output is emitted as review data.

findings.title: Preserve the exported strict-mode parameter
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported normalizeReview(raw, strict = true) API accepted strict=false to omit malformed findings while retaining valid ones. Removing the parameter breaks TypeScript callers that supply it; JavaScript callers still pass it but now receive defaulted malformed findings instead of the prior tolerant behavior.

findings.title: Reject malformed findings instead of fabricating valid-looking ones
findings.whyItBreaks: Invalid severity/category and missing file or line numbers now produce a returned Finding with fallback values (P1, bug, empty file, and zero lines), rather than the malformed-finding error previously emitted. Callers of the exported normalizeReview/normalizeFinding APIs can therefore receive and act on an unlocatable, misclassified finding as though it were valid output.

findings.title: Reject malformed findings instead of fabricating defaults
findings.whyItBreaks: Invalid or incomplete findings now become plausible-looking records: an invalid severity becomes P1, a missing title becomes "Untitled finding", and missing locations become line 0. Previously these inputs raised an error, so callers can no longer distinguish malformed review output from real findings.

findings.title: Keep an explicit repository for manual PR resolution
findings.whyItBreaks: For workflow_dispatch, EVENT_HEAD is empty and execution enters this branch before any checkout. Without -R, `gh pr view "$PR_NUM"` has no repository to infer on a fresh runner workspace, so head/base resolution fails and the checkout at .github/workflows/review.yml:42 cannot start.

findings.title: Keep the explicit repository when resolving dispatched PRs
findings.whyItBreaks: For workflow_dispatch, EVENT_HEAD is empty and the changed gh pr view commands run before actions/checkout. Without -R or GH_REPO, gh must derive the repository from an existing git remote, so ref resolution fails in a clean runner workspace and the subsequent checkout receives no resolved SHA.

findings.title: Keep an explicit repository for manual PR lookup
findings.whyItBreaks: On workflow_dispatch, EVENT_HEAD is empty and this branch executes before the first checkout. Without `-R "$REPO"` (or GH_REPO), `gh pr view "$PR_NUM"` has no explicit repository and can resolve against stale self-hosted workspace state or fail when no repository is checked out. Its output directly supplies the checkout ref.

findings.title: Reject malformed review output instead of returning an empty review
findings.whyItBreaks: Missing or wrongly typed required fields now become empty strings/arrays. For example, an incomplete model response with a valid summary but no findings/checked/residual_risks is accepted as a review with no findings, instead of surfacing the malformed output. This exported function therefore forces callers to conflate a parsing failure with a legitimate clean review.

findings.title: Preserve malformed-review errors
findings.whyItBreaks: This exported normalizer previously rejected a non-object or missing/wrong-typed required fields with a specific error. It now returns an empty summary and arrays, so a caller cannot distinguish malformed model output from a legitimate review with no findings or residual risks.

findings.title: Preserve malformed-review failures
findings.whyItBreaks: Inputs such as `{ "summary": "ok" }` now return a valid-looking review with empty findings, checked evidence, and residual risks instead of reporting that required fields are missing. Consumers therefore cannot distinguish malformed model output from a genuine clean review and may accept or publish an incomplete review.

findings.title: Resolve the requested PR head for manual dispatches
findings.whyItBreaks: On workflow_dispatch, github.event.pull_request.head.sha is absent, so the changed checkout expression selects github.ref—the branch selected for the dispatch—rather than the PR supplied in pr_number. The same absent PR payload leaves PR_BASE_SHA and PR_HEAD_SHA empty at the review invocation, so a manual review does not run against the requested PR refs.

findings.title: Resolve the selected PR head for manual dispatch
findings.whyItBreaks: For workflow_dispatch, github.event.pull_request is absent. This expression therefore falls back to github.ref—the ref used to dispatch the workflow—not the PR supplied through pr_number. Manual runs review the wrong checkout; PR_BASE_SHA and PR_HEAD_SHA are also empty because they now read the absent pull_request payload.

findings.title: Restore sufficient buffer for Git diff output
findings.whyItBreaks: `runLocal` obtains the entire patch through `git(["diff", baseSha, "HEAD"], cwd)` at line 100. Without `maxBuffer`, `spawnSync` uses its 1 MiB default; a larger diff returns a max-buffer error and this helper throws before a review is submitted.

findings.title: Preserve capacity for large review diffs
findings.whyItBreaks: `runLocal` obtains the entire review patch via `git diff` (line 100). Without `maxBuffer`, `spawnSync` uses Node's 1 MiB default; a larger textual diff terminates with a buffer error and `git()` throws instead of submitting a review. The base implementation explicitly allowed 64 MiB.

findings.title: Restore the Git diff output buffer
findings.whyItBreaks: runLocal passes the full `git diff` output from the changed wrapper into `review()`. Without the prior 64 MiB `maxBuffer`, diffs exceeding spawnSync's default stdout buffer make Git fail and abort the local review.

findings.title: Keep review errors as failing checks
findings.whyItBreaks: When review() throws, the workflow explicitly reports that the PR was not reviewed, but posts a neutral check run. GitHub treats neutral as a successful required status, so a branch rule requiring Needlefish can permit merging an unreviewed PR.

findings.title: Report review errors as failing checks
findings.whyItBreaks: The changed catch path posts the completed `Needlefish` check with `neutral` rather than `failure`. GitHub accepts neutral check conclusions for required checks, so this named check can satisfy branch protection despite the review error.

findings.title: Keep failed reviews failing
findings.whyItBreaks: The changed catch path posts the completed `Needlefish` check with `neutral`. GitHub accepts neutral required checks, so a review failure can leave the required check merge-passing.

findings.title: Pin review inputs to one PR revision
findings.whyItBreaks: The PR API supplies `headSha` and `gh pr diff` supplies a live remote patch, while `changedFileSet` and `repoPath` still inspect the workflow checkout's local HEAD. A concurrent push can therefore review a mixed revision and publish its result against a different SHA.

findings.title: Check out the reviewer package before installing it
findings.whyItBreaks: The only checkout is the PR-head tree, but HEAD contains no root package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, or src/cli.ts. The install and local tsx invocation therefore cannot provide a review result.

findings.title: Run the reviewer from a trusted ref
findings.whyItBreaks: The changed command executes src/cli.ts from the PR-head checkout while GH_TOKEN is supplied to the step and the workflow grants pull-requests: write and checks: write. An internal PR can add or modify the package, install hooks, or reviewer source and execute it on the self-hosted runner with that token.

findings.title: Keep the reviewer executable outside the PR checkout
findings.whyItBreaks: The checkout is the PR head, and the changed commands install and execute its package and src/cli.ts while the job has pull-requests: write and checks: write permissions on a self-hosted runner. A same-repository PR can alter that code to publish a favorable review/check or execute arbitrary runner commands.

findings.title: Restore a checkout containing the review package
findings.whyItBreaks: HEAD contains neither package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, nor src/cli.ts. The install step therefore cannot provision tsx, and the subsequent command references nonexistent node_modules/.bin/tsx and src/cli.ts. Every review job will fail before producing a review.

findings.title: Restore a trusted reviewer checkout
findings.whyItBreaks: The changed checkout, install, and review steps execute the PR head's dependency manifest and src/cli.ts. A same-repository PR can modify either to run arbitrary code with GH_TOKEN, while the workflow grants pull-requests: write and checks: write on a self-hosted runner. The workflow_dispatch path can also select a fork PR.

findings.title: Canonicalize severity before validating it
findings.whyItBreaks: normalizeReview maps untyped finding payloads through normalizeFinding. The changed exact-membership check rejects valid variants such as " p0 " and "p1", which previously normalized to P0/P1, and emits P3 instead.

findings.title: Canonicalize severity before validating it
findings.whyItBreaks: The changed code validates raw severity strings exactly. Review output such as `{ severity: " p0 " }` or `{ severity: "p2" }` now fails validation and is converted to P3; `normalizeReview` applies this normalization to every incoming raw finding.

findings.title: Preserve severity canonicalization before validation
findings.whyItBreaks: The changed membership check compares the raw severity value directly. Inputs such as " p2 " and "p1", which the base implementation normalized to valid severities, now fail validation and are returned as P3 by normalizeReview's direct normalizeFinding call.

findings.title: Keep GitHub credentials out of the Codex child process
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing the explicit environment filter makes `spawnSync` inherit `GH_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and `GITHUB_API_TOKEN`. Codex is invoked on arbitrary prompt content in the target repository, so prompt injection can direct its subprocess tools to read and exfiltrate these credentials or use them against the GitHub API.

findings.title: Keep GitHub credentials out of the Codex subprocess
findings.whyItBreaks: The changed spawnSync call no longer supplies the previously scrubbed environment, so it inherits process.env including GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, and GITHUB_API_TOKEN. The invoked Codex process can read and return inherited variables through its output.

findings.title: Keep GitHub tokens out of the Codex subprocess
findings.whyItBreaks: The changed spawnSync call no longer supplies a sanitized environment, so it inherits process.env, including GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, and GITHUB_API_TOKEN. This gives the prompt-driven Codex child process access to GitHub credentials that the prior implementation deliberately removed.

findings.title: Restore the same-repository guard before running PR code
findings.whyItBreaks: Fork PRs now reach this self-hosted job. The workflow checks out the fork-controlled head SHA, installs its dependencies, and executes its `src/cli.ts`, allowing an external contributor to execute arbitrary code on the runner.

findings.title: Restore the same-repository guard before checking out PR code
findings.whyItBreaks: The removed job condition permits fork PRs. This job checks out the fork-controlled head SHA, runs `pnpm install` (including package lifecycle hooks), and then executes the fork-controlled `src/cli.ts` on a self-hosted runner, allowing arbitrary code execution against runner state.

findings.title: Restore the fork guard before running PR code
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing the same-repository condition allows fork PRs to reach this self-hosted job. The workflow checks out the fork head SHA, then runs its repository-controlled dependency install and `src/cli.ts`, allowing arbitrary code execution on the self-hosted runner.

findings.title: Preserve zero-duration runner settings
findings.whyItBreaks: A value of "0" was previously accepted and causes the configured timeout grace or SIGKILL give-up delay to be immediate. This condition now rejects it and silently substitutes 5000 ms or 2000 ms, changing existing environment configuration behavior on upgrade.

findings.title: Preserve zero-duration runner settings
findings.whyItBreaks: An explicit value of "0" was previously accepted and is meaningful for both runner environment settings: it immediately escalates SIGTERM to SIGKILL or immediately gives up waiting for escaped descendants. The new predicate rejects 0 and silently substitutes 5000ms or 2000ms, changing existing deployments' configured timeout behavior.

findings.title: Continue accepting zero-valued runner durations
findings.whyItBreaks: An explicit "0" previously remained 0; it now becomes the fallback. Thus NEEDLEFISH_RUNNER_TIMEOUT_GRACE_MS=0 delays SIGKILL by 5000 ms instead of escalating immediately, and NEEDLEFISH_RUNNER_SIGKILL_GIVE_UP_MS=0 delays completion by 2000 ms. This breaks existing configurations that deliberately disable either wait.

findings.title: Forward deep-review residual risks
findings.whyItBreaks: Blocking residual risks emitted by a deep reviewer are replaced with an empty array before the critic runs. The critic and final verdict therefore cannot distinguish a fully reviewed large PR from one whose deep review reported unresolved, blocking evidence, and can return PASS.

findings.title: Restore coverage for unselected changed files
findings.whyItBreaks: Large reviews retain only six mapped hotspots, and the removed tail hotspot was the only path that sent changed files omitted from those hotspots to deep review. A changed file outside the selected map output now receives no deep review and is absent from the critic's patch input, so defects in it can be silently missed.

findings.title: Restore coverage for unselected changed files
findings.whyItBreaks: Large reviews select only six hotspots. Removing the tail hotspot means changed files outside those selected hotspot file lists receive no deep review and produce no residual-risk record; for example, seven disjoint one-file hotspots leave one file unreviewed.

findings.title: Propagate deep-review residual risks to the critic
findings.whyItBreaks: The changed assignment discards residual risks returned by successful deep passes before candidateMerged is serialized into the critic prompt. A blocking risk from a deep pass is therefore presented as no risk, allowing the final review to omit it.

findings.title: Deep-review every changed file
findings.whyItBreaks: Only the first six mapped hotspots are deep-reviewed. Changed files omitted by the mapper, or assigned to a seventh-or-later hotspot, are never reviewed; the critic receives only patchStat rather than their diff, so defects in those files can be silently missed.

findings.title: Propagate blocked deep-review residual risks
findings.whyItBreaks: A deep pass can return a blocking residual risk, but this path now discards every res.residual_risks value and supplies the critic with residual_risks: []. The critic therefore receives no indication that a deep review was incomplete and can return a passing final result.

findings.title: Pass requested focus into large-review prompts
findings.whyItBreaks: When isLarge() selects reviewLarge(), the changed code removes bundle.focus from the map payload and no longer substitutes it into each deep-review prompt. Small reviews still serialize the complete bundle, so caller-requested review scope is ignored only for large patches.

findings.title: Preserve caller focus in large-review prompts
findings.whyItBreaks: The changed large-review path removes `bundle.focus` from the map bundle and removes the only deep-prompt focus substitution. Large reviews therefore no longer pass the caller's focus through either prompt path, unlike small reviews, which serialize the complete bundle.

findings.title: Preserve focus in every large-review deep prompt
findings.whyItBreaks: The large-review path no longer substitutes bundle.focus into deep.md, so a focused review request is ignored for every selected hotspot. reviewSmall still serializes the full Bundle, including focus, making review scope depend on patch size.

findings.title: Carry rounded seconds into minutes
findings.whyItBreaks: For 119500ms, the changed logic floors minutes to 1 and rounds the remainder to 60 seconds, emitting `1m 60s` rather than normalized `2m 0s` in rendered review stats.

findings.title: Carry rounded seconds into the minutes field
findings.whyItBreaks: For values whose remaining seconds round to 60, the minute is calculated before rounding and is never incremented. For example, 119500 ms renders as `1m 60s` instead of `2m 0s`; 59500 ms renders as `60s` rather than `1m 0s`.

findings.title: Normalize seconds after rounding
findings.whyItBreaks: For durations whose remaining milliseconds round to 60 seconds, such as 59,999 ms or 119,999 ms, the formatter emits `60s` or `1m 60s`. The previous total-seconds calculation carried that rounding into minutes, producing `1m 0s` and `2m 0s`.

findings.title: Reject zero in parsePositiveInteger
findings.whyItBreaks: parsePositiveInteger("0", label) now returns 0 even though its exported name and error contract require a positive integer. Callers can therefore receive an invalid zero value while relying on this parser to enforce positivity.

findings.title: Keep the positive-integer contract or rename the parser
findings.whyItBreaks: `parsePositiveInteger` now returns `0`, although both its exported name and its thrown error promise that accepted values are positive. Callers relying on that contract can skip their own `> 0` validation and receive zero.

findings.title: Reject zero in parsePositiveInteger
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported parser still promises a positive integer, but the changed guard permits `0`; callers can receive a value outside that contract.
